newsitem.title: FRANCE: Brigitte Bardot to pay damages to ex-husband, son.
newsitem.headline: Brigitte Bardot to pay damages to ex-husband, son.

text.p: A French court on Wednesday ordered former film star Brigitte Bardot to pay damages to her son and to one of her ex-husbands for branding their baby a "tumour" and his father a "vulgar macho" in her best-selling memoirs.

The court ordered Bardot, 62, and publishing house Grasset to pay 150,000 francs ($26,000) to ex-husband Jacques Charrier and 100,000 francs ($17,000) to their son Nicholas, 36, for comments made about them in the book "Initiales B.B.".
But the court, while recognising the image of the two men was sullied, rejected their requests that Bardot's memoirs be excised of 80 pages mentioning them.
The book, running to almost 600 pages, has sold 600,000 copies in French. It has been translated into 15 other languages.

The case against Bardot, now an animal rights campaigner, said she invaded the privacy of the two men with such passages as one in which she recounted feeling suicidal after she learned she was pregnant with Nicolas and in which she described him as "a tumour feeding off me".

The often bitter autobiography branded ex-husband Charrier, an actor-turned-producer who was married to Bardot from 1959 to 1963, "a vulgar, dictatorial and uncontrolled macho, a gigolo, alcoholic and despicable".
Bardot's lawyer argued that the life of the one-time national icon was part of French history and writings about historical events could not be banned.
